themes.title: Wall Street grades AI capex: Alphabet -10%, Microsoft rewarded
themes.summary: Alphabet shares fell about 10% after Google admitted its 'AI mode' is cannibalizing traditional search while a $51bn AI outlay deepens cash burn, per the FT. Bloomberg adds that Alphabet's core-business sales missed across the board. In contrast, Microsoft's cloud sales beat estimates with capex held in check, and Oracle told investors its AI bet pays off sooner than expected - the market is now discriminating on AI spend-to-revenue conversion.
themes.angle: The AI capex cycle has a P&L referee: boards should grade spending on conversion, not capability.

themes.title: China's AI labs distill OpenAI's Astra outputs
themes.summary: The Information reports OpenAI's Astra has become the top distillation target for Chinese labs, with Moonshot AI and DeepSeek leaning on its outputs for the models they released this month. Export controls are policing chips and weights, but not the knowledge locked in model outputs. The story reframes the US-China AI contest as a training-data and inference-economics battle rather than a hardware one.
themes.angle: Chips are export-controlled; logits are not - the distillation loophole is now the fulcrum of US-China AI policy.

themes.title: GCC AI buildout hits the cost-resilience test
themes.summary: AGBI reports rising data-centre construction costs are pressuring Saudi AI ambitions, while The Arab Weekly frames resilience as the Gulf's new test. Momentum remains: Dubai AI Campus doubled its 2030 target to 1,000 firms after early traction past $270M, and Snowflake plans $300M in Saudi investment through 2030. Global AI leaders are also converging on Dubai as the emirate expands its ambitions.
themes.angle: The Gulf is entering phase two of its AI story: from ambition-setting to cost-and-resilience management.

themes.title: Anthropic ships Claude 5.5 family, files for IPO
themes.summary: Anthropic's newsroom shows a Claude 5.5 generation: Opus 5.5 leads agentic coding and costs about 40% less to run than Opus 5, with Sonnet 5.5 and Haiku 5.5 also upgraded. Separately, the company filed an S-1 with the SEC for a proposed IPO and pledged a portion of its shares to a public-benefit fund whose stake grows with the company. It is the clearest sign yet that frontier labs are moving to public markets amid the capex debate.
themes.angle: Cheaper frontier inference plus an IPO prospectus: Anthropic is betting efficiency wins the boardroom.

themes.title: DeepMind ships Gemini 4 Carbon, Genie 4 gains audio
themes.summary: Google DeepMind released Gemini 4 Carbon roughly two weeks after Argon, and it took the #1 spot on Artificial Analysis, per The Decoder and Dealroom. The Information confirms it is Google's second major model launch in a month. In parallel, Genie 4 previews real-time world generation with native audio and live steering - a step toward interactive, media-native AI systems rather than text-only assistants.
themes.angle: Two flagship launches in a month is model-cadence escalation - and a direct counter-punch to the capex critics.

themes.title: The agentic enterprise takes shape
themes.summary: OpenAI expanded its ServiceNow partnership to bring models and agents into enterprise workflows, and published a 'future of the firm' essay on how AI enters the org chart. The FT argues AI agents need middle managers too, and Amazon is hedging against AI shopping agents by adding 250 million outside listings, per The Information. Enterprises are designing around agents - and agents are forcing commerce and workflow redesigns in return.
themes.angle: Agentic AI is moving from pilots to org-chart and supply-chain design decisions - the real enterprise story of 2026.

themes.title: AI cyber: 'Black October' fizzles, encryption fears rise
themes.summary: Axios reports the cybersecurity world braced for 'Black October' after AI found critical flaws in the web's foundational code - but millions of automated attacks have so far yielded few successes, a Y2K-like anticlimax. The Information says AI-found bugs have still sparked a corporate security spending spree, and the FT warns AI's growing mathematical prowess is forcing a rethink of encryption security once dominated by the quantum threat.
themes.angle: The AI cyber scare didn't land - but it already moved budgets, and the encryption clock has started ticking.

themes.title: OpenAI plans to buy Google's AI chips
themes.summary: The Information reports OpenAI - a longtime Nvidia customer - plans to buy Google's AI chips to expand computing capacity, a story picked up by Reuters and others. The move would diversify OpenAI away from Nvidia and validate Google's TPU line as merchant silicon. It is a meaningful signal in the inference-economics and chip-supply wars.
themes.angle: OpenAI buying Google silicon reshuffles the compute supply chain - a quiet but structural hedge.

themes.title: AI infrastructure M&A and compute buildout accelerate
themes.summary: Marvell is in advanced talks for a megadeal to buy data-centre optics maker Lumentum, per Bloomberg, and TPG is pursuing a $5bn acquisition of UK data-centre group Ark. FuriosaAI quadrupled its valuation to $2.9bn chasing Nvidia, while Nscale's CEO pushes a $30bn neocloud IPO. Equinix says project barriers boost its pricing power, and Samsung is hiking spending after a chip profit miss on resurgent AI demand - the compute buildout is consolidating and repricing.
themes.angle: Compute is consolidating into winners: expect optics, neoclouds and data-centre operators to reprice.

themes.title: ADGM issues first regional crypto-mining guidance
themes.summary: Abu Dhabi Global Market published dedicated guidance making crypto mining a licensable commercial activity - the first international financial centre in the region to do so, per Economy Middle East and Gulf Business. The move signals ADGM positioning itself as the compliance-friendly venue for compute-heavy digital-asset and AI infrastructure businesses in the GCC.
themes.angle: Licensing crypto miners is ADGM's play to capture compute-heavy digital infrastructure - a regional-first regulatory signal.
